note: Iraq's national spirits. The ones with `start` describe the situation on 1 January 2000 and cite sources; the others are granted by focuses and decisions. Values are gameplay estimates.

spirits.name: UN sanctions
spirits.description: A comprehensive UN embargo has been in force since August 1990 and stays tied to disarmament.

spirits.name: Oil-for-Food
spirits.description: Under a UN programme set up in 1995, Iraq sells oil in controlled quantities for food, medicine and humanitarian goods.

spirits.name: No-fly zones
spirits.description: The United States and the United Kingdom enforce no-fly zones over the north and south, proclaimed after the 1991 war.

spirits.name: Vast oil reserves
spirits.description: Iraq holds the world's fifth largest proven oil reserves.

spirits.name: War-damaged economy
spirits.description: The Iran-Iraq War damaged the infrastructure, and the 1991 war and the sanctions hit the economy further.

spirits.name: Sectarian divide
spirits.description: Distrust between Shia, Sunni and Kurdish communities shapes politics and security.

spirits.name: National reconciliation
spirits.description: Power sharing and amnesties narrow the divides between communities.

spirits.name: Power shortages
spirits.description: Generation cannot meet demand at the summer peak.

spirits.name: Reliable power
spirits.description: New plants and gas capture keep the lights on.

spirits.name: Oil boom
spirits.description: Contracts with foreign companies raise production and exports.

spirits.name: Popular Mobilization Forces
spirits.description: Paramilitary factions formally part of the armed forces under the prime minister.
